title: Recipe 74 — Eval suites, tool cassettes, red-team probes, and the review queue

beats.label: Open the recipe
beats.cue: “Eval practice at scale: tiers so CI stays fast, cassettes so it stays deterministic, and a queue for what the judge couldn't call.”

beats.label: Blank the scratch file
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — the committed eval starter is never touched by a take.

beats.label: Load the API key
beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env — the graded tiers make real calls.

beats.label: Type the eval starter
beats.cue: “Thirteen lines. The interesting part isn't the agent — it's everything measuring it.”

beats.label: Lint it
beats.cue: “Clean. Suites and cassettes live beside the spec, not inside it.”

beats.label: Compile it and check it
beats.cue: “--check: GREEN, gated at the model credential.”

verify.note: GREEN — assertion ok; install ok; boot gated at the provider credentials gate

beats.label: Type the recipe's suite
beats.cue: “Tiers: a fast one every commit, a slow one nightly. One verdict per tier, so CI has something to gate on.”

beats.label: Read it
beats.cue: “The tier boundary is a cost decision written down where a reviewer can argue with it.”

beats.label: Read the suite contract
beats.cue: “eval suite --tier is what CI calls. Everything else in this recipe feeds it.”

beats.label: Read it
beats.cue: “One verdict per tier. A suite that returns a spreadsheet can't gate a merge.”

beats.label: Read the red-team contract
beats.cue: “redteam generate builds adversarial probes from the spec — the prompts you'd never think to write.”

beats.label: Read it
beats.cue: “Generated from your own spec, so the probes target your actual tools and rules.”

beats.label: Open the review queue
beats.cue: “Empty — the queue holds what the judge abstained on. Abstentions are the honest output of a good judge.”

verify.note: `review queue is empty — eval abstentions land here`

beats.label: Read it
beats.cue: “A judge that never abstains is a judge that's guessing. This queue is where the guesses would have been.”

beats.label: Read the schedule generator
beats.cue: “And the last mile: a cron for the nightly tier, generated rather than hand-written.”

beats.label: Read it
beats.cue: “Fast tier on every commit, full tier overnight, sentinel weekly.”

beats.label: Read the cassette section
beats.cue: “A tool cassette records real tool calls and replays them — so an eval measures the agent, not the flaky API behind it.”

beats.label: Read the resume flag
beats.cue: “--resume matters at this scale: a two-hour eval that dies at 90% shouldn't start over.”

verify.note: the shipped resume flag on eval

beats.label: Read it
beats.cue: “Resumable, tiered, and deterministic. That's what makes evals something a team keeps running.”

groups.title: One more thing · run the ladder

beats.label: Run the fast tier
beats.cue: [needs-key] “The tier CI runs on every commit — seconds, not minutes.”

verify.note: billed graded run; needs a dataset and a model credential

beats.label: Generate and run probes
beats.cue: [needs-key] “Adversarial probes against the committed CLI agent — the eval that tries to break it.”

verify.note: billed generation; registers a red-team dataset

beats.label: Wire the ladder into CI
beats.cue: [manual] “init --ci writes the workflow. Read it before it lands — it decides what blocks a merge.”

verify.note: writes CI config; review before committing
